review_scope: Temperature semantics and proposed Planck-weighting lookup coverage only; no generation, model run, or source edit.

ice_index_input.meaning: Pinned static Warren-Brandt ice-Ih refractive-index compilation

source_findings.finding: The Mie refractive-index function index_at(wavenumber) interpolates the static input by wavelength and has no temperature argument.
LW temperature changes the Planck source weights, proportional to nu^3/expm1(c2*nu/T), used in the band integration; SW uses solar weights.
The output metadata explicitly labels LW temperature as Planck source weighting only and the material index as static ice-Ih.

proposed_temperature_axis_K.judgment: Reasonable candidate lookup coverage for the observed 179.996 K table-range failure, provided runtime remains bounded to this explicit range and does not clamp or extrapolate. This is a denser numerical sampling of Planck weighting, not a temperature-dependent optical-constant model.

scientific_limitations: The fixed Warren-Brandt ice-Ih refractive index remains unchanged at every temperature; the wider axis does not validate its physical applicability across 150-330 K.
The 233 K node is retained for continuity with the prior table; inspected source does not establish it as a special material calibration knot.
A 5 K spacing is not itself an interpolation error bound. No accuracy or forecast-readiness claim follows from coverage alone.

The table remains an experimental homogeneous spherical ice-Ih PSD treatment. It does not validate graupel or hail optics, habits, porosity, wet growth/coatings, mixed phase, or a temperature-dependent ice refractive index.
required_numerical_followup_before_claim: Evaluate direct generator values at independent between-node temperatures, including points near 179.996 K and both table boundaries, across representative lambda slopes and bands; compare with lookup interpolation and report field-specific errors without tuning a pass threshold after seeing results.
Keep strict out-of-range rejection and record the supported temperature interval in table/runtime metadata.
Treat these checks as interpolation verification under the fixed material/kernel only, not empirical validation of the ice/graupel/hail model.
